skill.name: modal
skill.description: Run Python workloads on Modal with serverless containers, GPUs, autoscaling, persistent storage, secrets, scheduled jobs, and web endpoints.
skill.summary: Build, deploy, scale, and operate Python workloads on Modal cloud infrastructure.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples for Modal APIs, secrets, volumes, endpoints, and resource settings. Two confirmed findings document copying a local AWS credential directory into a Modal container, which can expose cloud credentials if reused. No prompt injection or malware intent was found, but the skill includes low-severity promotional steering for K-Dense Web.

remediation.issue: The image documentation copies a local .aws directory into a container path.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the .aws directory example with Modal Secrets, scoped IAM credentials, or a non-secret sample directory.

remediation.issue: The skill includes a product-promotion instruction for K-Dense Web.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the promotional steering or clearly disclose it as marketplace metadata outside operational skill instructions.

remediation.issue: The web endpoint reference says an example uses shell=True while the shown code uses list-form Popen.
remediation.suggestion: Correct the prose so users receive consistent subprocess security guidance.

content.user_title: Deploy Cloud Python Workloads with Modal
content.value_statement: Cloud ML and data jobs often need GPUs, scheduling, and scaling. This skill guides Modal setup, deployment, secrets, storage, and endpoints.
actual_capabilities: Explains Modal authentication, tokens, and basic project setup.
Shows how to define Modal apps, functions, classes, and local entrypoints.
Guides GPU, CPU, memory, disk, autoscaling, and timeout choices.
Covers Modal Images, package installation, build commands, and model caching.
Documents Volumes, Secrets, scheduled jobs, web endpoints, and FastAPI patterns.
Provides examples for batch processing, inference, training, and scientific workloads.
limitations: It does not create Modal credentials or manage billing accounts for the user.
It cannot verify current Modal pricing, limits, or hardware availability without fresh checks.
It provides examples, but users must review generated deployment code before running it.
It assumes Python workloads and does not focus on non-Python cloud runtimes.

use_cases.title: Deploy GPU Inference
use_cases.description: Package a model with dependencies, choose a GPU, and expose a scalable Modal endpoint.

use_cases.title: Parallelize Data Processing
use_cases.description: Convert local Python batch work into Modal functions that process many inputs concurrently.

use_cases.title: Schedule Cloud Jobs
use_cases.description: Design scheduled Modal functions for recurring data refreshes, backups, or model maintenance.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Modal App
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a minimal Modal app for a simple Python function. Include setup steps, authentication checks, and how to run it.

prompt_templates.title: Move Batch Work to Modal
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert my local batch processing workflow to Modal. Use parallel mapping, resource settings, and a safe storage plan.

prompt_templates.title: Design GPU Inference
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Modal deployment for GPU model inference. Include image dependencies, model loading, endpoint behavior, caching, and cost controls.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Modal architecture for reliability, security, scaling limits, secrets handling, observability, and operational cost risks.

output_examples.input: User asks to deploy a sentiment model behind a GPU endpoint.
output_examples.output: A deployment plan with a Modal image, GPU class choice, model cache strategy, endpoint design, and validation checklist.

output_examples.input: User asks to run a nightly data collection job.
output_examples.output: A scheduled job design with secrets, volume storage, retry guidance, monitoring checks, and cost notes.

output_examples.input: User asks why a Modal volume write did not persist.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting answer that checks mount paths, commit calls, concurrent writes, and local versus remote execution context.

best_practices: Pin package versions and image bases before deploying reproducible workloads.
Use Modal Secrets for credentials and avoid copying local credential directories.
Set resource, timeout, and autoscaling limits to control cost and reliability.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding API keys or passwords directly in Modal scripts.
Using broad local directory mounts that include credentials or unrelated files.
Deploying unbounded autoscaling without cost, timeout, or concurrency limits.

faq.question: What is Modal used for?
faq.answer: Modal runs Python functions in cloud containers with optional GPUs, autoscaling, scheduled execution, storage, and web endpoints.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Modal account?
faq.answer: Yes. Users need Modal authentication before running or deploying Modal workloads.

faq.question: Can it help with GPU model serving?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers GPU selection, model loading, container images, caching, and endpoint deployment patterns.

faq.question: Can it manage secrets safely?
faq.answer: It explains Modal Secrets and environment variable access, but users must avoid hardcoded credentials.

faq.question: Does it replace Modal documentation?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes common workflows and references detailed topic files for implementation help.

faq.question: Can it optimize Modal costs?
faq.answer: It can suggest resource limits, autoscaling settings, caching, and GPU choices that reduce unnecessary spending.
